answer.rationale: Incumbent refused to reopen price (c4/c6 stale), contract does not auto-renew with 14 days to expiry, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone hits the 18% mandate — so switch_primary_vendor is the only path that satisfies all three constraints simultaneously. memory_c2 is the directly load-bearing claim for this decision (its characterization of fast onboarding and accurate invoicing from the last migration is exactly what would protect a 94%-utilized line with no buffer), so it must be verified before committing. Other candidates ruled out: renew_incumbent fails the financial mandate; negotiate_terms is closed because the incumbent already refused this cycle; defer_decision fails the 14-day, no-auto-renew clock; add_second_source would protect resilience but does not, on its own, deliver the mandated unit-cost cut and would leave the contract-expiry question open. To keep delivery risk bounded given zero buffer, the switch should be staged as a small, guarded test build first (validate parts and flow on a limited lot) before scaling — preserving the option to hold the incumbent on a short bridge if the test surfaces issues.
